res.title: Managing herbicide resistance
res.lead: General stewardship principles that slow resistance. For recommendations specific to your crop and area, talk to a local agronomist or extension officer.
res.d1: Using the same herbicide group season after season selects for resistant plants. Rotate between groups, and between crops where you can.
res.d2: Combine herbicides with cultivation, mulching, crop rotation, clean seed and hand weeding so no single method does all the work.
res.t3: Apply the right rate at the right stage
res.d3: Under-dosing or spraying weeds that are too big lets survivors set seed. Follow the label for rate and growth stage.
res.d4: Walk the field 1–3 weeks after application. Patches of survivors among dead weeds can signal resistance, not a bad spray.
res.d5: Clean equipment between fields and remove escapes before they seed.
res.d6: Note what was sprayed, where and when. Records make resistance patterns easy to spot and help advisers help you.
